methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective analysis (2001-2019, n=157 screened, 154 analyzed) of Ph+ B-ALL treated with pediatric-inspired PM-DFCI protocol + imatinib. Analyses use appropriate tools: Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, univariate/multivariable Cox with alloSCT as time-varying covariate (important to avoid immortal-time bias with transplant). Stratification by era (2001-2009, 2010-2015, 2016-2019) links protocol changes to outcomes. Key weaknesses: very small subgroups (23 non-alloSCT patients in 2016-2019 cohort driving headline 87% 4-year OS), significant era confounding (supportive care, disease monitoring, and TKI generation all improved over time), no cytogenetic/molecular subgroup data (IKZF1, ABL kinase mutations), no external validation, and secular trends cannot be fully separated from protocol effects. Authors acknowledge retrospective-bias and molecular-data limitations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective single-center case series spanning 18 years maps to Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality cohort/case series). Clinical relevance is real and timely: the paper directly addresses whether routine CR1 alloSCT is needed in Ph+ B-ALL treated with pediatric-inspired chemotherapy + TKI when MRD-guided, and the MRD-driven non-transplant arm's 87% 4-year OS compares favorably with EBMT-registry transplant cohorts (73-77%). Supports emerging guideline positions (NCCN 2024) and contributes to the ongoing transplant debate. Not practice-changing alone but a meaningful contribution to a real clinical question.

reporting_quality.justification: As a retrospective observational cohort, STROBE applies. Reporting covers patient selection, protocol description with supplementary figures, outcome definitions (BCR::ABL1 MRD criteria, RFS/OS), and statistical methods with multivariable Cox. Era stratification with hazard ratios and CIs is presented for key comparisons. Weaknesses: no sample-size or power considerations, no description of missing data handling, no reporting of how continuous time-varying covariates were specified beyond alloSCT, and limited cytogenetic/molecular characterization. Supplementary tables referenced for additional detail. Data and code are not shared.

novelty_literature.justification: The question of whether CR1 alloSCT is necessary in Ph+ B-ALL with TKI + chemotherapy is actively debated in the literature, with recent reports (Ravandi, Short, Badar, Jabbour, D-ALBA, GIMEMA ALL2820) moving toward MRD-guided, non-transplant approaches. This work provides a real-world single-institution 18-year experience with the specific PM-DFCI pediatric-inspired protocol + imatinib, with era-based stratification linking asparaginase omission and alloSCT de-escalation to improving outcomes. Novelty is incremental but meaningful given the long follow-up and specific protocol lineage.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is clearly written, well-organized, and appropriate for a hematology readership. Clinical rationale is well-articulated and evolves logically from institutional experience to broader implications. Figures (time period stratification, alloSCT vs non-alloSCT K-M curves) and tables communicate the key comparisons effectively. Limitations are acknowledged, though the discussion could more systematically address era-confounding (supportive care, imaging). One small REDACTED placeholder in results.

key_strengths: Long 18-year single-institution cohort with consistent pediatric-inspired PM-DFCI backbone, enabling temporal analysis of specific protocol changes
AlloSCT modeled as time-varying covariate, appropriately addressing immortal-time bias in transplant comparisons
MRD-guided non-transplant subgroup (2016-2019) achieves 87% 4-year OS, directly comparable to EBMT registry transplant outcomes
Transparent exposition of iterative protocol changes and their rationale, grounded in institutional experience
key_concerns: Very small era subgroups (23 non-alloSCT patients in 2016-2019) generate wide CIs and limit confidence in headline survival estimates
Era confounding (supportive care, monitoring, TKI generation improvements) cannot be disentangled from specific protocol changes
No cytogenetic/molecular subgroup analysis (IKZF1, kinase mutations) which are known prognostic factors
Retrospective single-center design limits generalizability; no external validation
Blinatumomab-based frontline regimens (D-ALBA, GIMEMA ALL2820) may render the compared paradigm increasingly obsolete
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically relevant real-world data with appropriate time-varying analysis, but small era subgroups and unaddressed confounders limit strength of conclusions. Fits Tier 3 with minor revisions.
